탱고북 오리지널 · 시리즈물

탱고북 삼국지

도원결의에서 오장원까지 50년을 24권으로 · 초등 저학년 그림책
24권 (시리즈 완결)
94장
17⭐ 하이라이트
24권 대본 완성
약 610~750컷 (1권 실측 장당 6.4장면)

1 · 이 라인은 무엇인가

시리즈물이다. 호리 3라인·전래동화가 「한 권이 한 이야기」인 것과 달리, 삼국지는 1권부터 24권까지 인물이 늙어 가며 이어지는 한 편이다. 그래서 다른 라인에 없는 제약이 셋 붙는다.

  • 읽는 순서가 있다 — 라이브러리에서 권 번호 순으로 배열하고 표지에도 번호를 넣는다.
  • 인물이 늙는다 — 같은 얼굴을 50년에 걸쳐 그린다. 그 해법이 samgukji-cast.md 다.
  • 한 그림체로 끝까지 간다 — 창작동화처럼 권마다 바꿀 수 없다.

대상은 초등 저학년이다. 탱고북 본진(4~7세)보다 위이고 「타임 티코」와 같은 자리다.

2 · 그림체 — 수묵 산수 위의 5.5등신

🔴 출처는 우리 자산이다 — C:/projects/threekingdoms(영걸전형 SRPG)에서 이미 렌더까지 나온 하우스 스타일을 그림책으로 옮겼다. 앞서 만들었던 후보 셋(그림자극·연환화·형지염색)은 렌더가 하나도 없는 설계도여서 폐기했다. 분석 전문 = docs/art-direction/samgukji-anchor.md.

정체 — 두 층으로 되어 있다

배경은 젖은 수묵 산수, 인물은 그 위에 얹은 굵은 먹 윤곽의 5.5등신(2026-08-20 에 4등신에서 올렸다 — 4등신 시안이 세 번 다 「애 같다」로 돌아왔다).
  • 🔴 두 층의 마감이 달라서 「눈은 가장 마감된 것으로 간다」가 저절로 성립한다 — 인물이 늘 그 쪽에서 가장 마감된 것이다.
  • 🔴 관우의 얼굴이 실제로 붉다(SD 시트 실측 #6C4836 계열) — 얼굴색 축이 이 그림체에서 성립하는 것을 렌더로 확인했다.
  • 🔴 전원 5.5등신이라 키로는 아무도 못 가른다 → 개체는 어깨 폭(머리 폭의 몇 배)으로 가른다. 동탁 2.6 ↔ 조조 1.5.
  • 팔레트는 렌더에서 뽑았다 — 종이 #F0E2C0·먹 #2B2B2B·올리브 #485A48·황토 #D8B46C·가죽 #5A4836.
  • ⚠️ 법적 라인 상속 — 코에이 그래픽·일러스트 스타일 모방 금지, 「영걸전」 명칭 금지(NOT 절에 박아 두었다).
🎨 STYLE ANCHOR samgukji-inkwash-sd
앵커 전문 보기
STYLE ANCHOR - samgukji-inkwash-sd

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PALETTE (muted earth, sampled from the house renders)
paper #F0E2C0 · ink #2B2B2B · olive-green #485A48 · pale jade #5A6C5A · ochre #D8B46C ·
mustard #6C6C48 · leather brown #5A4836 · deep brown #483624 · skin #D8B4A2.
ACCENTS, USED SPARINGLY: vermilion #B8352A · gold #C9A227.
🔴 KERCHIEF YELLOW #E8B233 IS THE REBEL HOST'S AND NOBODY ELSE'S. Book 1's hero fights that host:
yellow on him reads as one of them. It happened once in test; do not put it back.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for that person, comes from their CHARACTER SHEET.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill any figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must be that person from the
  sheet. If the silhouette does not say who it is, the figure is wrong.

CANVAS
16:9 double-page spread. 🔴 NO lettering, numerals, signage or captions anywhere in the image, in any
script. No caption band - the picture runs to all four edges. Light is warm and low, from one side.
🔴 THE SKY IS NEVER BLUE: it is the warm paper, washed ochre where the sun is.

STAGE CLAUSES (carry only the clause that page needs)
- VILLAGE/MARKET: thatched roofs and a fence in wash, one pine, an earth road; ground = one wash band.
- PALACE/COURT: repeated pillars and roof brackets receding into mist.
- FIELD/BATTLE: hills and mist above; below, the repeated silhouette host and a few banners.
- ROAD/JOURNEY: one road, one or two pines, the rest wash and bare paper.

NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.
첫 시험 — 쪽 컷을 뽑기 전에 이 셋을 먼저 굽고 승인받는다.
  • 관우 — 붉은 얼굴이 이 등신에서도 성립하는가
  • 장비 — 삐죽삐죽한 수염 윤곽이 큰 머리에서 뭉개지지 않는가
  • 유비 — 🔴 큰 귀가 큰 머리에 묻히지 않는가(가장 위험한 조합)

아래 §4 캐스트 카드의 「📋 시트 프롬프트 복사」가 앵커까지 붙은 완성본을 내놓는다 — 그대로 붙여넣으면 된다.

3 · 지금 열려 있는 결정

🎨 그림체 — 위 셋 중 하나를 골라야 다음이 굴러간다.
SCENE 의 매체 어휘(획·판·워시)가 그림체에서 나오므로, 정해지기 전에 쓴 콘티는 그 부분만 비워 둔다. 1권 대본이 그렇게 쓰여 있다 — 컷·장소·인물·배경·톤 다섯은 확정이고 매체 한 줄만 비었다.
🩸 후반부 순화 기준.
1권에서 쓴 방식은 결과만 보여 주기다(쓰러진 사람 대신 주인 없는 말과 떨어진 투구, 매질 대신 닫힌 문). 다만 관우의 최후(20권)·장비의 죽음(21권)·백제성(21권)은 주인공이 죽는 장면이라 같은 처리로 덮이지 않는다. 🔴 20권에 닿아서 정하면 늦다. (A안을 고르면 「퇴장」이 그 답이 된다.)
📚 파닉스 연동은 하지 않는다. 핵심단어가 「청룡언월도」·「연환계」라 파닉스 단원과 안 맞는다. 읽기 전용 라인으로 둔다.

4 · 캐릭터 — 얼굴색이 배역을, 수염 길이가 나이를 말한다

원칙 1 · 시그니처는 절대 고정 — 색·소품·외모는 나이와 옷이 바뀌어도 그대로.

원칙 2 · 나이와 옷은 권 번호가 정한다 — 사람마다 단계 수가 다르다(유비 5, 관우 3, 사마의 2). SSOT 는 build-samgukji.mjs 의 STAGES 이고, 쪽 발주서에는 그 권 한 줄만 나간다.

원칙 3 · 의상은 신분이 오를 때만 — 날씨·기분·장면으로 바꾸지 않는다. 바꾸면 같은 사람이 매 쪽 달라진다.

🔴 단계가 있는 인물은 시트가 여러 장이고, 붙여넣기 칸도 그만큼이다 — 아래 카드의 권 범위 칸에 각각 넣는다. 칸이 하나면 20권 발주에 1권 얼굴이 첨부된다. 🔴 단계가 셋 넘는 인물은 대표 한 장을 먼저 승인한 뒤 나머지를 그 승인본에서 파생시킨다(얼굴을 글로 두 번 만들면 두 사람이 된다).

🔴 개체 규격 SSOT = docs/art-direction/samgukji-cast.md — 얼굴색·수염·실루엣·키·악센트 다섯 축과 검사 조항이 거기 있다. 아래 카드는 그 파일에서 굽는다.

시트는 여기 한 곳에만 붙여넣고, 회차 대본은 이름으로만 참조한다(24권마다 같은 시트를 다시 붙이지 않는다). 🔴 [공통 스타일 앵커] 자리는 그림체가 확정되면 실제 앵커로 치환된다.

유비 Liubei 촉 시트 5장
캐릭터 시트 프롬프트 보기
Draw a character reference sheet. This is not a page from the book.
🔴 NOTHING IS ATTACHED AND NOTHING NEEDS TO BE. Every value you need is written below - face,
  build, clothing, colours, proportion. Do not ask for a reference image; this prompt is it.

🔴 PROPORTION, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE - the figure is 5.5 HEADS TALL. Measure it: the height of the
  head from crown to chin, taken five and a half times, is the whole standing height. Lightly
  stylised, NOT chibi and NOT realistic: the head is a little large, the body compact, and the legs
  carry it. 4 heads makes a grown man read as a child; 8 makes a fashion plate.
  It applies to every full figure on this sheet, including the black silhouette.

🔴 CANVAS: one image, 3:2 landscape, flat warm-paper ground (#F0E2C0). No landscape, no ink-wash
  hills, no mist, no scenery. Nothing behind the figures.

🔴 THERE IS NO WRITING IN THIS PICTURE. Not a title, not a label under a head, not a word beside a
  figure, not a measurement, not a colour code, in any script. 🔴 THE WORDS IN THIS PROMPT ARE
  INSTRUCTIONS AND MUST NEVER BE COPIED ONTO THE IMAGE - a previous attempt lettered my own headings
  onto the sheet. If you are about to draw a letter, stop: this is not an annotated model sheet.

Arrange it like this. Across the top, the same figure standing three times at the same height in the
same costume, seen from the front, from three-quarters, and from the side. To the right of them, the
head alone, large, seen from the front, and beneath that the head alone seen from the side. Across
the middle, the head four more times, showing in turn a calm face, an angry face, a grieving face
and a laughing face. Along the foot, the whole figure once more, filled in solid black with no
interior detail at all, so that only the outline remains. Every one of those parts must be present.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Liubei   (bake this FIRST)
LIUBEI - the eldest brother, the one the other two follow. SHOULDERS = 1.7 head-widths across.
FACE: 🔴 UNPAINTED. His is one of four bare faces in this book and the only one that is bare AND
  has a moustache. Broad, calm, wide-set eyes, a mouth that rests almost closed.
🔴 EARS: THE LARGEST EARS IN THE BOOK - each ear is as tall as from his eyebrow to his chin, and
  they stand clear of the head on both sides so that they BREAK HIS OUTLINE. Blacked out, the ears
  are how you know him.
ARMS: long - his fingertips reach below the knee when he stands with arms down.
🔴 TWO SWORDS, ONE ON EACH HIP - he is the only figure in this book carrying two blades. They stay
  through every costume stage, including the king's robe.
🔴 THE BLADES ARE HAN JIAN AND NOT KATANA - this has come back wrong twice, so draw them from these
  measurements: STRAIGHT, no curve at all; the same width from guard to near the tip, then a short
  symmetrical point; a FLAT RING at the end of the grip instead of a pommel cap; a small oval guard,
  not a round plate. Scabbard plain wood, no lacquer, no cord wrapping. 🔴 EACH ONE HANGS FROM THE
  BELT ON TWO SHORT CORDS with the blade pointing down - neither is pushed edge-up through the sash,
  and neither is slung on a strap across the chest or back.
🔴 ACCENT: A VERMILION SASH AT THE WAIST (#B8352A). It survives EVERY stage below, and no one else
  in this book wears a sash of that colour. 🔴 IT WAS YELLOW UNTIL A TEST RENDER - and yellow is the
  rebel host's colour, so with a head cloth on he read as one of the men he fights in book 1.
  Vermilion also suits him: he is Han royal kin, and the Han honoured red.

AGES & COSTUMES - 5 stages. 🔴 DO NOT DRAW THEM ALL IN THIS IMAGE. At this scale
tall the faces come out small, and a sheet with 5 rows of them will drift into 5 different people.
🔴 BAKE THIS SHEET WITH ONE STAGE ONLY - the one marked PRIMARY below. Approve it. Then generate each
remaining stage as its own small sheet, feeding the APPROVED image back in as the reference, and asking
only for FRONT VIEW + HEAD CLOSE-UP. The face is never generated twice from text.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)

  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.

  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

  has a moustache. Broad, calm, wide-set eyes, a mouth that rests almost closed.
🔴 EARS: THE LARGEST EARS IN THE BOOK - each ear is as tall as from his eyebrow to his chin, and
  they stand clear of the head on both sides so that they BREAK HIS OUTLINE. Blacked out, the ears
  are how you know him.
ARMS: long - his fingertips reach below the knee when he stands with arms down.
🔴 TWO SWORDS, ONE ON EACH HIP - he is the only figure in this book carrying two blades. They stay
  through every costume stage, including the king's robe.
🔴 THE BLADES ARE HAN JIAN AND NOT KATANA - this has come back wrong twice, so draw them from these
  measurements: STRAIGHT, no curve at all; the same width from guard to near the tip, then a short
  symmetrical point; a FLAT RING at the end of the grip instead of a pommel cap; a small oval guard,
  not a round plate. Scabbard plain wood, no lacquer, no cord wrapping. 🔴 EACH ONE HANGS FROM THE
  BELT ON TWO SHORT CORDS with the blade pointing down - neither is pushed edge-up through the sash,
  and neither is slung on a strap across the chest or back.
🔴 ACCENT: A VERMILION SASH AT THE WAIST (#B8352A). It survives EVERY stage below, and no one else
  in this book wears a sash of that colour. 🔴 IT WAS YELLOW UNTIL A TEST RENDER - and yellow is the
  rebel host's colour, so with a head cloth on he read as one of the men he fights in book 1.
  Vermilion also suits him: he is Han royal kin, and the Han honoured red.

STYLE ANCHOR - samgukji-inkwash-sd

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for this person, is written out below - there is no other
  sheet to consult, because this prompt is what makes it.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill the figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must say who this is. If the
  silhouette does not, the figure is wrong.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Guanyu   (bake this FIRST)
GUANYU - the second brother, and the tallest figure in the book. SHOULDERS = 2.0 head-widths.
🔴 FACE: DEEP JUJUBE RED, a flat even red across the whole face and neck. HE IS THE ONLY RED FACE
  IN THIS BOOK. It never changes - not with age, not with weather, not with lamplight.
EYES: long and narrow, the outer corners lifted; heavy level brows above.
🔴 BEARD - THE CLOCK OF THIS BOOK: youth = it reaches his CHEST. prime = it reaches BELOW HIS CHEST.
  old = it reaches HIS NAVEL and pale hairs run through it. It hangs as ONE mass, never in strands,
  and he strokes it with the back of his hand.

  every pose. Carried, never sheathed.

🔴 SILHOUETTE: blacked out, one hanging mass at the chest and one long shaft over the shoulder.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

🔴 KERCHIEF YELLOW #E8B233 IS THE REBEL HOST'S AND NOBODY ELSE'S. Book 1's hero fights that host:
yellow on him reads as one of them. It happened once in test; do not put it back.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for this person, is written out below - there is no other
  sheet to consult, because this prompt is what makes it.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill the figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must say who this is. If the
  silhouette does not, the figure is wrong.



NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Zhugeliang · from book 14
ZHUGELIANG - the strategist. 🔴 SHOULDERS = 1.4 head-widths, THE NARROWEST FIGURE IN THE BOOK.
  Enters in book 12 and never wears armour.
FACE: 🔴 UNPAINTED, and the narrowest face in the book. Level brows, eyes half-lidded and calm,
  a small closed mouth that rests in a faint smile. He is never drawn shouting.
HEAD: a soft cloth band tied around the head, its two short ties hanging at the back.
🔴 HIS HANDS: ONE HAND ALWAYS HOLDS A WHITE FEATHER FAN, in all thirteen books he appears in.
  🔴 HE IS THE ONLY ADULT IN THIS BOOK WHO NEVER HOLDS A WEAPON. That is the whole point of him.
COSTUME: ONE robe for thirteen books - a wide pale crane-robe with sleeves that hang past the hands.
  🔴 HIS RANK NEVER CHANGES, SO HIS CLOTHES NEVER CHANGE. He is the only fixed costume in the book.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: blacked out, a tall smooth column with wide hanging sleeves and ONE fan shape held
  out from the body. He is the only figure with no weapon line anywhere in his outline.

THIS STAGE ONLY: 서른둘. 두건이 없어진다. 옷은 그대로. 짧고 곧게 다듬은 검은 턱수염.

🔴 Draw all five items listed in TASK above.
🔴 THIS IS THE PRIMARY SHEET - approve it before generating the other stages.

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:

  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.

  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM

  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.

  soldier, general   - a helmet

    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.

  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)

  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.

  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.

  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:

  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.

  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.

    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow

  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet

    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

🔴 ACCENT: GOLD - rings, buckles, the fittings of his belt. He is the only figure wearing gold
  ornaments, and there are 🔴 AT MOST 5 GOLD PIECES ON HIM in any one picture.

SIMAYI - the last opponent, and the one who outlives everybody. SHOULDERS = 1.5 head-widths.

  in a picture with either of them he sits between the two. Long and narrow.
EYES: 🔴 HALF-CLOSED IN EVERY PICTURE, even when he is surprised. He is the only figure in this book
  whose eyes are never fully open. Brows level and low.
BEARD: narrow and long, hanging straight down in one thin fall; grey-flecked in book 24.
🔴 HIS HANDS ARE INSIDE HIS SLEEVES unless he is giving an order - so his outline has no arms, just
  a column with two sleeve-ends meeting at the front. Where Zhugeliang's sleeves hang open with a
  fan held out, his are closed and empty.
COSTUME: one grey-black robe and armour set for three books. His rank does not visibly change.
🔴 ACCENT: NONE - he is the only figure in this book with no accent colour anywhere. That absence is
  the design: the man who wins is the one nothing marks.

  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun

  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.

  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

🔴 KERCHIEF YELLOW #E8B233 IS THE REBEL HOST'S AND NOBODY ELSE'S. Book 1's hero fights that host:
yellow on him reads as one of them. It happened once in test; do not put it back.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for this person, is written out below - there is no other
  sheet to consult, because this prompt is what makes it.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill the figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must say who this is. If the
  silhouette does not, the figure is wrong.



NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Liuxie   (bake this FIRST)
LIUXIE - the younger brother, nine years old, who becomes the emperor of the rest of this book.
SHOULDERS = 1.2 head-widths.
🔴 HE IS DRAWN BESIDE THE CHILD EMPEROR AND MUST NOT BE MISTAKEN FOR HIM. Both are small, both are
  in oversized clothes. What separates them is ONE THING AND IT IS NOT CLOTHING:
  🔴 THE OLDER BOY'S BACK IS BENT AND THIS ONE'S BACK IS STRAIGHT. Draw the spine, not the face.
FACE: bare, thin, a mouth that stays closed. He answers when spoken to.
COSTUME: a prince's plain robe, also too big, but he has gathered the sleeve in one fist so his
  hand shows. 🔴 ONE VISIBLE HAND is the second thing that separates the two boys.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

  stylised, NOT chibi and NOT realistic: the head is a little large, the body compact, and the legs
  carry it. 4 heads makes a grown man read as a child; 8 makes a fashion plate.
  It applies to every full figure on this sheet, including the black silhouette.

Arrange it like this. Across the top, the same figure standing three times at the same height in the
same costume, seen from the front, from three-quarters, and from the side. To the right of them, the
head alone, large, seen from the front, and beneath that the head alone seen from the side. Across
the middle, the head four more times, showing in turn a calm face, an angry face, a grieving face
and a laughing face. Along the foot, the whole figure once more, filled in solid black with no
interior detail at all, so that only the outline remains. Every one of those parts must be present.

STYLE ANCHOR - samgukji-inkwash-sd

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

the middle, the head four more times, showing in turn a calm face, an angry face, a grieving face

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for this person, is written out below - there is no other
  sheet to consult, because this prompt is what makes it.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill the figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must say who this is. If the
  silhouette does not, the figure is wrong.



NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

LVBOSHA - the old man at the farmhouse. SHOULDERS = 1.5 head-widths.
FACE: bare, soft, deeply wrinkled around the eyes from smiling. A thin white beard to the collarbone.
COSTUME: a farmer's padded coat, one shoulder patched with a different cloth.
🔴 WHAT READS: A WINE JAR CARRIED IN BOTH ARMS AGAINST HIS CHEST, big enough that he must lean back

🔴 SILHOUETTE: a round mass at chest height held by two arms - unmistakable, and it is the last
  thing the reader sees of him.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

🔴 NOTHING IS ATTACHED AND NOTHING NEEDS TO BE. Every value you need is written below - face,
  build, clothing, colours, proportion. Do not ask for a reference image; this prompt is it.

🔴 PROPORTION, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE - the figure is 5.5 HEADS TALL. Measure it: the height of the
  head from crown to chin, taken five and a half times, is the whole standing height. Lightly
  stylised, NOT chibi and NOT realistic: the head is a little large, the body compact, and the legs
  carry it. 4 heads makes a grown man read as a child; 8 makes a fashion plate.
  It applies to every full figure on this sheet, including the black silhouette.

🔴 CANVAS: one image, 3:2 landscape, flat warm-paper ground (#F0E2C0). No landscape, no ink-wash
  hills, no mist, no scenery. Nothing behind the figures.

🔴 THERE IS NO WRITING IN THIS PICTURE. Not a title, not a label under a head, not a word beside a
  figure, not a measurement, not a colour code, in any script. 🔴 THE WORDS IN THIS PROMPT ARE
  INSTRUCTIONS AND MUST NEVER BE COPIED ONTO THE IMAGE - a previous attempt lettered my own headings
  onto the sheet. If you are about to draw a letter, stop: this is not an annotated model sheet.

Arrange it like this. Across the top, the same figure standing three times at the same height in the
same costume, seen from the front, from three-quarters, and from the side. To the right of them, the
head alone, large, seen from the front, and beneath that the head alone seen from the side. Across
the middle, the head four more times, showing in turn a calm face, an angry face, a grieving face
and a laughing face. Along the foot, the whole figure once more, filled in solid black with no
interior detail at all, so that only the outline remains. Every one of those parts must be present.

STYLE ANCHOR - samgukji-inkwash-sd

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PALETTE (muted earth, sampled from the house renders)
paper #F0E2C0 · ink #2B2B2B · olive-green #485A48 · pale jade #5A6C5A · ochre #D8B46C ·
mustard #6C6C48 · leather brown #5A4836 · deep brown #483624 · skin #D8B4A2.
ACCENTS, USED SPARINGLY: vermilion #B8352A · gold #C9A227.
🔴 KERCHIEF YELLOW #E8B233 IS THE REBEL HOST'S AND NOBODY ELSE'S. Book 1's hero fights that host:
yellow on him reads as one of them. It happened once in test; do not put it back.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for this person, is written out below - there is no other
  sheet to consult, because this prompt is what makes it.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill the figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must say who this is. If the
  silhouette does not, the figure is wrong.



NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Lijue   (bake this FIRST)
LIJUE - one of the two officers left over when their master falls. SHOULDERS = 1.7 head-widths.
🔴 HE IS ALWAYS DRAWN WITH GUOSI AND THE TWO MUST NOT BE INTERCHANGEABLE:
  LIJUE IS THE TALLER, and his eyebrows are so pale they nearly vanish - 🔴 a face with almost no
  brow line. He stands upright.
FACE: bare, square, a wide flat nose.
COSTUME: campaign armour with no decoration, a cloak stiff with dust.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: of the pair, the tall straight one.
🔴 ACCENT: none.
곽사 Guosi 군웅

CHARACTER SHEET - Taoqian   (bake this FIRST)
TAOQIAN - the old governor who has to give his province away. SHOULDERS = 1.3 head-widths.
FACE: bare, hollowed, a sparse white beard through which the chin shows. Eyes wet at the lower lid
  in every panel, without weeping.
🔴 THE BODY IS THE CHARACTER: he is drawn SEATED in all but one panel, and when seated his back
  makes a curve, not a line. 🔴 HIS HANDS SHAKE - draw the seal he offers with both hands, because
