NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

FACE: bare, handsome, a beard combed to a clean point and 🔴 EYEBROWS THAT SLOPE DOWN AT THE OUTER

  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.

  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.

  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

mustard #6C6C48 · leather brown #5A4836 · deep brown #483624 · skin #D8B4A2.
ACCENTS, USED SPARINGLY: vermilion #B8352A · gold #C9A227.
🔴 KERCHIEF YELLOW #E8B233 IS THE REBEL HOST'S AND NOBODY ELSE'S. Book 1's hero fights that host:
yellow on him reads as one of them. It happened once in test; do not put it back.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for this person, is written out below - there is no other
  sheet to consult, because this prompt is what makes it.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill the figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must say who this is. If the
  silhouette does not, the figure is wrong.



NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Sunjian   (bake this FIRST)
SUNJIAN - the tiger of the east. SHOULDERS = 1.9 head-widths.
FACE: bare, square, a short hard beard cut straight across the bottom. Eyes wide open.
🔴 THE RED HEADSCARF IS THIS MAN. It is tied at the back with two ends hanging to the shoulder
  blade, and it moves in every panel. 🔴 IT IS THE ONLY RED IN A PANEL HE STANDS IN.
🔴 HIS SON WILL WEAR THIS SCARF FROM BOOK 7. In book 4 the two appear together and the son does NOT
  have it yet - that absence is deliberate and must not be drawn in.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a compact body under a head with two ribbons streaming off the back of it.
🔴 ACCENT: THE RED SCARF.

Draw a character reference sheet. This is not a page from the book.
🔴 NOTHING IS ATTACHED AND NOTHING NEEDS TO BE. Every value you need is written below - face,
  build, clothing, colours, proportion. Do not ask for a reference image; this prompt is it.

🔴 PROPORTION, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE - the figure is 5.5 HEADS TALL. Measure it: the height of the
  head from crown to chin, taken five and a half times, is the whole standing height. Lightly
  stylised, NOT chibi and NOT realistic: the head is a little large, the body compact, and the legs
  carry it. 4 heads makes a grown man read as a child; 8 makes a fashion plate.
  It applies to every full figure on this sheet, including the black silhouette.

🔴 CANVAS: one image, 3:2 landscape, flat warm-paper ground (#F0E2C0). No landscape, no ink-wash
  hills, no mist, no scenery. Nothing behind the figures.

🔴 THERE IS NO WRITING IN THIS PICTURE. Not a title, not a label under a head, not a word beside a
  figure, not a measurement, not a colour code, in any script. 🔴 THE WORDS IN THIS PROMPT ARE
  INSTRUCTIONS AND MUST NEVER BE COPIED ONTO THE IMAGE - a previous attempt lettered my own headings
  onto the sheet. If you are about to draw a letter, stop: this is not an annotated model sheet.

Arrange it like this. Across the top, the same figure standing three times at the same height in the
same costume, seen from the front, from three-quarters, and from the side. To the right of them, the
head alone, large, seen from the front, and beneath that the head alone seen from the side. Across
the middle, the head four more times, showing in turn a calm face, an angry face, a grieving face
and a laughing face. Along the foot, the whole figure once more, filled in solid black with no
interior detail at all, so that only the outline remains. Every one of those parts must be present.

STYLE ANCHOR - samgukji-inkwash-sd

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

CHARACTER SHEET - Huaxiong   (bake this FIRST)
HUAXIONG - the gate-keeper nobody can pass. SHOULDERS = 2.1 head-widths.
🔴 HIS FACE IS DARK RED AND GUANYU'S FACE IS RED, AND THEY MEET IN BOOK 3. This is the most
  dangerous pair in the book. Separate them like this and only like this:
  🔴 GUANYU: a FLAT EVEN red, the same value across the whole face, no shadow. Long narrow eyes.
  🔴 HUAXIONG: a BROWNISH red that is DARKER IN THE HOLLOWS - and 🔴 CHEEKBONES THAT STICK OUT far
    enough to catch a highlight. Guanyu has no bone showing anywhere.
  If a reader must check the beard to tell them apart, the faces are wrong.
BEARD: short, black, bristling sideways - nothing hangs.
🔴 HELMET: a fringe of animal fur around the rim. Guanyu wears no helmet, ever.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a wide block with a shaggy crown; Guanyu is a tall column with one long shaft.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

SIMAHUI - the old scholar who tells Liubei he has no people. SHOULDERS = 1.4 head-widths.
🔴 HE WEARS WHITE AND SO DOES ZHUGELIANG, AND THEY ARE ONE BOOK APART. Separate them:
  🔴 THIS MAN IS OLD - a white beard to the chest, and Zhugeliang's beard is short, dark and cut
    square at the chin. 🔴 THIS MAN HAS NO FAN. The fan belongs to the other one and to no one else.
FACE: bare, round, 🔴 SMILING IN EVERY PANEL so that the eyes are two curves and the pupils barely
  show. He does not stop smiling even when he refuses to answer.
COSTUME: an undyed scholar's robe, sleeves wide enough to swallow both hands.
🔴 HANDS: TUCKED INTO THE OPPOSITE SLEEVES. He is never drawn pointing at anything - that is the
  character: he tells Liubei what is wrong and will not tell him where to go.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a soft column with no hands showing and no object anywhere on it.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PALETTE (muted earth, sampled from the house renders)
paper #F0E2C0 · ink #2B2B2B · olive-green #485A48 · pale jade #5A6C5A · ochre #D8B46C ·
mustard #6C6C48 · leather brown #5A4836 · deep brown #483624 · skin #D8B4A2.
ACCENTS, USED SPARINGLY: vermilion #B8352A · gold #C9A227.
🔴 KERCHIEF YELLOW #E8B233 IS THE REBEL HOST'S AND NOBODY ELSE'S. Book 1's hero fights that host:
yellow on him reads as one of them. It happened once in test; do not put it back.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for this person, is written out below - there is no other
  sheet to consult, because this prompt is what makes it.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill the figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must say who this is. If the
  silhouette does not, the figure is wrong.



NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Xushu   (bake this FIRST)
XUSHU - the first strategist Liubei ever has, and the one he loses. SHOULDERS = 1.5 head-widths.
FACE: bare, young, NO BEARD - 🔴 he is the only man in a strategist's robe with a bare chin.
COSTUME: a plain civil robe with sleeves narrower than a court official's, because he walks.
🔴 THE HANDS COUNT THINGS. In every panel one hand is doing something with number: fingers half
  folded, a tally on a strip of bamboo, three stones set on a table. 🔴 Never an empty gesture.
POSTURE: leans forward from the waist when he is thinking; stands upright only when he is leaving.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a narrow figure bent slightly at the middle, one hand raised to chest height with the
  fingers spread and not closed.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

Draw a character reference sheet. This is not a page from the book.
🔴 NOTHING IS ATTACHED AND NOTHING NEEDS TO BE. Every value you need is written below - face,
  build, clothing, colours, proportion. Do not ask for a reference image; this prompt is it.

🔴 PROPORTION, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE - the figure is 5.5 HEADS TALL. Measure it: the height of the
  head from crown to chin, taken five and a half times, is the whole standing height. Lightly
  stylised, NOT chibi and NOT realistic: the head is a little large, the body compact, and the legs
  carry it. 4 heads makes a grown man read as a child; 8 makes a fashion plate.
  It applies to every full figure on this sheet, including the black silhouette.

🔴 CANVAS: one image, 3:2 landscape, flat warm-paper ground (#F0E2C0). No landscape, no ink-wash
  hills, no mist, no scenery. Nothing behind the figures.

🔴 THERE IS NO WRITING IN THIS PICTURE. Not a title, not a label under a head, not a word beside a
  figure, not a measurement, not a colour code, in any script. 🔴 THE WORDS IN THIS PROMPT ARE
  INSTRUCTIONS AND MUST NEVER BE COPIED ONTO THE IMAGE - a previous attempt lettered my own headings
  onto the sheet. If you are about to draw a letter, stop: this is not an annotated model sheet.

Arrange it like this. Across the top, the same figure standing three times at the same height in the
same costume, seen from the front, from three-quarters, and from the side. To the right of them, the
head alone, large, seen from the front, and beneath that the head alone seen from the side. Across
the middle, the head four more times, showing in turn a calm face, an angry face, a grieving face
and a laughing face. Along the foot, the whole figure once more, filled in solid black with no
interior detail at all, so that only the outline remains. Every one of those parts must be present.

COSTUME: a governor's robe of good cloth, the knees smoothed flat from sitting.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a low wide triangle. Everyone else in his room is a vertical.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

CHARACTER SHEET - Adou   (bake this FIRST)
ADOU - the infant carried out of an army. SHOULDERS: not applicable - he is a bundle.
🔴 HE IS THE ONLY FIGURE IN THIS BOOK WHOSE FACE IS NEVER FULLY SHOWN. At most one cheek, one closed
  eye and one fist appear above the cloth. Never two eyes.
🔴 THE BUNDLE IS ALWAYS THE SAME SIZE - as long as a grown man's forearm and no longer, so that
  Zhaoyun's armour can close over it.
CLOTH: undyed, wrapped so that one corner hangs free and moves.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a smooth oval with one loose corner. It must read as a bundle, not as a sack.
🔴 ACCENT: none - 🔴 he must NOT be a bright spot in the panel. He is what everyone is looking for,
  and the reader should have to look for him too.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Liushan   (bake this FIRST)
LIUSHAN - Adou grown up, and the last king of his father's country. SHOULDERS = 1.6 head-widths.
🔴 HE HAS HIS FATHER'S EARS - the same size, standing clear of the head, breaking the outline. That
  inheritance is the only reason this character reads at all.
🔴 AND EVERYTHING ELSE IS THE OPPOSITE OF HIS FATHER: the eyes are round and soft where Liubei's are
  wide-set and level; 🔴 THE MOUTH RESTS SLIGHTLY OPEN where his father's rests closed.
FACE: bare, round, no beard at any age.
🔴 NO WEAPON, EVER. Liubei carries two swords through every costume; this one carries nothing, and
  in the panel where the two stand together that difference is the page.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: his father's ears on a rounder, softer body.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

STYLE ANCHOR - samgukji-inkwash-sd

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for this person, is written out below - there is no other
  sheet to consult, because this prompt is what makes it.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill the figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must say who this is. If the
  silhouette does not, the figure is wrong.



NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

PANGTONG - the second of the two great strategists, and the one nobody looks at twice.
SHOULDERS = 1.6 head-widths.
🔴 NOT BEING HANDSOME IS THIS CHARACTER, AND IT MUST NOT TIP INTO UGLINESS OR COMEDY. Build it from
  three measurements and no adjectives:
  🔴 the nose is SHORT AND BLUNT, ending above the line of the mouth corners;
  🔴 the hairline sits ONE FINGER LOWER than everyone else's, so the forehead is small;
  🔴 the hair is not combed - three or four strands stand away from the head in every panel.
🔴 AND THE EYES ARE THE BRIGHTEST IN THE BOOK: larger than Zhugeliang's, with a clear highlight.
  Draw the eyes last and draw them best. The whole character is that the face is plain and the eyes
  are not.
COSTUME: a civil robe, the hem dusty, worn without a sash.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a compact figure with an uneven crown of hair.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.

  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

  sitting. Age is in the beard and the skin; it is never in the spine.
🔴 THE BOW: he is THE ONLY ADULT IN THIS BOOK WHO CARRIES A BOW. It is longer than he is tall and it
  is on him in every panel, strung, across the back or in the left hand.
COSTUME: old armour, plates darkened, worn over a plain coat.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a straight vertical with a long curve crossing it diagonally. Nobody else in this
  book has a curve in their outline.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun

  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

🔴 SILHOUETTE: a straight figure inside a slightly larger straight shape.
🔴 ACCENT: imperial yellow on the robe - 🔴 which no one may read as HIS colour. It is the office.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Anliang   (bake this FIRST)
ANLIANG - the champion sent first. SHOULDERS = 2.0 head-widths.
🔴 HE AND WENCHOU ARE A PAIR AND ARE TOLD APART BY THE NECK AND THE WEAPON:
  🔴 ANLIANG HAS ALMOST NO NECK - the helmet rim nearly touches the shoulder plates. A BROAD BLADE.
FACE: bare, wide, a thick black beard growing high on the cheek.
COSTUME: heavy northern armour with a fur collar.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a block with no gap between head and shoulders.
🔴 ACCENT: none.

Draw a character reference sheet. This is not a page from the book.
🔴 NOTHING IS ATTACHED AND NOTHING NEEDS TO BE. Every value you need is written below - face,
  build, clothing, colours, proportion. Do not ask for a reference image; this prompt is it.

🔴 PROPORTION, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE - the figure is 5.5 HEADS TALL. Measure it: the height of the
  head from crown to chin, taken five and a half times, is the whole standing height. Lightly
  stylised, NOT chibi and NOT realistic: the head is a little large, the body compact, and the legs
  carry it. 4 heads makes a grown man read as a child; 8 makes a fashion plate.
  It applies to every full figure on this sheet, including the black silhouette.

🔴 CANVAS: one image, 3:2 landscape, flat warm-paper ground (#F0E2C0). No landscape, no ink-wash
  hills, no mist, no scenery. Nothing behind the figures.

🔴 THERE IS NO WRITING IN THIS PICTURE. Not a title, not a label under a head, not a word beside a
  figure, not a measurement, not a colour code, in any script. 🔴 THE WORDS IN THIS PROMPT ARE
  INSTRUCTIONS AND MUST NEVER BE COPIED ONTO THE IMAGE - a previous attempt lettered my own headings
  onto the sheet. If you are about to draw a letter, stop: this is not an annotated model sheet.

Arrange it like this. Across the top, the same figure standing three times at the same height in the
same costume, seen from the front, from three-quarters, and from the side. To the right of them, the
head alone, large, seen from the front, and beneath that the head alone seen from the side. Across
the middle, the head four more times, showing in turn a calm face, an angry face, a grieving face
and a laughing face. Along the foot, the whole figure once more, filled in solid black with no
interior detail at all, so that only the outline remains. Every one of those parts must be present.

STYLE ANCHOR - samgukji-inkwash-sd

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PALETTE (muted earth, sampled from the house renders)
paper #F0E2C0 · ink #2B2B2B · olive-green #485A48 · pale jade #5A6C5A · ochre #D8B46C ·
mustard #6C6C48 · leather brown #5A4836 · deep brown #483624 · skin #D8B4A2.
ACCENTS, USED SPARINGLY: vermilion #B8352A · gold #C9A227.
🔴 KERCHIEF YELLOW #E8B233 IS THE REBEL HOST'S AND NOBODY ELSE'S. Book 1's hero fights that host:
yellow on him reads as one of them. It happened once in test; do not put it back.

CHARACTER DESIGN LANGUAGE
- 🔴 EVERY PERSON IS 5.5 HEADS TALL - head height taken five and a half times is the standing
  height. Lightly stylised, not chibi: head a little large, body compact, legs carrying it. 🔴 4
  reads as a child, 8 as a fashion plate. It never changes with rank or age.
- 🔴 THE FACE COLOUR IS THE CASTING AND NEVER CHANGES - not with light, weather or age; one steady
  tone. 🔴 WHICH tone, and every other value for this person, is written out below - there is no other
  sheet to consult, because this prompt is what makes it.
- Eyes = two strokes and a filled pupil; brows = one stroke and carry the expression. Mouths small.
  0 blush marks, 0 sparkle highlights, 0 sweat drops.
- 🔴 FEELING IS CARRIED BY THE WHOLE BODY: it leans, plants its feet wide, throws its arms out.
- 🔴 TEST: fill the figure solid and rub out the inside. What is left must say who this is. If the
  silhouette does not, the figure is wrong.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

NOT (rendering only)
airbrushing, glossy 3D, cel-shaded anime or manga screentone · photobash or photographic texture ·
🔴 Koei-style / Dynasty-Warriors-style character illustration, and Japanese sengoku armour ·
outlines on the landscape washes.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

🔴 AGE IS READ FROM THE FACE, NOT THE BODY - the proportion is 5.5 heads at every age, so the body
  cannot carry age. A beardless man is the hard case and this book has two of them (Liubei at 24, Zhaoyun
  at every age). Build the adult from FIVE measurements, all of them inside the head:
  1 EYE LINE at or above the middle of the head. A child's sits below it.
  2 EYES NARROW - width at least twice the height. A child's are round.
  3 THE HEAD IS TALLER THAN IT IS WIDE. A child's is as wide as it is tall.
  4 THE JAW HAS A CORNER under the ear and the chin comes to a plane, not a curve.
  5 THE NECK IS VISIBLE and as wide as the distance between the eyes. A child has no neck showing.
  🔴 TEST BEFORE YOU FINISH: could this face be a ten-year-old? Then it is wrong. "Semi-deformed"
  sets the proportion of the BODY and never makes the face a child's - the anchor says never chibi.

CHARACTER SHEET - Lusu   (bake this FIRST)
LUSU - the man in the middle who is honest with everyone. SHOULDERS = 1.6 head-widths.
FACE: bare, ROUND - 🔴 the roundest face among the adults of the east, where Zhouyu is angular and
  Sunquan is square. A short soft beard.
🔴 BOTH HANDS TUCKED INTO THE OPPOSITE SLEEVES in almost every panel, held at the waist. 🔴 HE IS
  DRAWN LISTENING: in two-person panels his head is turned toward the speaker and his mouth is shut.
COSTUME: a civil robe under a light travelling cloak - he is always just arrived or about to go.
🔴 SILHOUETTE: a soft column with no hands and no object; distinguished from Simahui by AGE (this
  man has a dark beard) and by the CLOAK (Simahui has none).
🔴 ACCENT: none.

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic
linework, muted earth tones, rice-paper texture in the washes, wide empty space. NOT photorealistic,
NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.

PERIOD - LATE HAN. These override anything "ancient Asian" suggests by default.
🔴 HAIR IS NEVER CUT. Grown men keep it long and bind it into a topknot at the crown. A shaved head,
  a cropped modern cut and a Japanese chonmage are all wrong.
🔴 THE TOPKNOT IS COVERED, and what covers it gives the rank:
  poorest, day-labourer - NOTHING. A bare topknot bound with a cord or a wooden pin. 🔴 THIS IS THE
    SAFE CHOICE and the one to take when in doubt.
  commoner with a trade - ZE (幘): a cloth cap that COVERS THE WHOLE CROWN and is knotted at the back,
    so the topknot is a bump UNDER the cloth. 🔴 IT IS A CAP, NOT A HEADBAND. A band around the brow
    with the topknot standing out above it is the Yellow Turban rebels' look and nobody else's.
  official, scholar  - a stiff dark cap set over it
  soldier, general   - a helmet
  🔴 An officer or an official with his head bare has just been beaten or pulled out of bed. That
    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.
🔴 THE ROBE CLOSES LEFT OVER RIGHT AS THE WEARER SEES IT - the collar reads as a y running from the
  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.
🔴 DRESS SAYS RANK, never mood or weather:
  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.
  official - a robe to the instep with wide sleeves. general - that robe worn under armour.
🔴 SLEEVES ARE NARROW ON EVERY WORKING FIGURE. Wide sleeves belong to court and study only.
🔴 NOT kimono, and this is the failure to watch for: no wide folded-back cuffs, no obi, no Japanese
  armour, no blade slung across the back.
🔴 THE SWORD IS A HAN JIAN, NOT A KATANA: the blade is STRAIGHT and double-edged, the same width for
  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM

    does not apply to a labourer, whose head is bare as a matter of course.

  wearer's left shoulder down to the right hip. The other way round is how a corpse is dressed.

  poorest - SHUHE (裋褐), the working dress of Han commoners: a coarse undyed hemp tunic whose hem
    falls BETWEEN HIP AND KNEE, worn OVER TROUSERS, cloth wraps on the shins, a rope belt, straw
    sandals. 🔴 IT IS A TUNIC AND TROUSERS, NOT A ROBE. Sleeves are NARROW - a wide sleeve cannot
    be worked in, and a floor-length robe reads as a gentleman, which he is not yet.

  most of its length, and the pommel is a flat ring or disc. No curve, no long two-hand grip, no
  round guard plate, no lacquered scabbard with a cord wrap. 🔴 It HANGS AT THE HIP ON CORDS FROM
  THE BELT, blade down - never thrust edge-up through a sash, never crossed behind the shoulders.

STYLE: A picture book for 7-9 year olds retelling the Three Kingdoms. THE WORLD IS PAINTED AS EAST
ASIAN INK-WASH LANDSCAPE; THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWN AS LIGHTLY STYLISED FIGURES LAID ON IT. Calligraphic

NOT anime-cel, NOT a 3D render.

RENDERING (finish hierarchy)
- 🔴 TWO LAYERS, FINISHED DIFFERENTLY. BACKGROUND = wet ink wash on warm paper: hills, pines, mist,
  sky; 0 outlines, drying into bare paper. FIGURES = clean ink outline of even weight, flat fill, ONE
  step of soft shading. A figure is always the most finished thing on its page.
- FINISHED THINGS PER PAGE = 2 - the person the page is about, and the one thing they handle.
- NAMED FIGURES IN FRONT = at most 3. 🔴 CROWDS AND ARMIES ARE NOT PEOPLE: ONE silhouette repeated
  12-40 times, smaller and paler as it recedes, dissolving into the mist.
- BACKGROUND OBJECT COUNT = at most 6 named things per page. Everything else is wash and bare paper.
- 🔴 MIST IS THE ERASER: distance is paler, not smaller; the far third of a wide shot dissolves into
  the paper. No hard horizon behind a figure.
- DENSITY RATION: only battle, market and court may fill the frame. Every other keeps AT LEAST HALF
  the frame as wash or bare paper. The scene brief names which is which.
